cases.why: consumer_lines is narrowed to a spelling the template never uses, so it returns [] for every token. The premise guard then reports '0 consumers, not one', which reads as a consumer having MOVED and sends the reader to re-trace a page that has not changed -- the same shape as a tool reading one number out of a multi-number summary and inventing a cause for the difference. Caught only by the companion that names a token whose uses must be found.

the count check is gutted, so a token can grow a second home while ACCEPTED_CLOSE goes on asserting the pair CANNOT MEET. That verdict is the whole reason this guard exists: give --accent-strong a second consumer on the Season Accuracy page and the two tokens are suddenly on one screen, with nothing in the suite saying so.

cases.why: the anchor check is gutted, so the one consumer may move anywhere and the premise still reads as holding. A single consumer is not enough on its own -- the verdict names WHICH element, because .srs-bar-fill is what confines --accent-strong to Power Ratings and Team Deep-Dive. Move that declaration onto a shared component and the count stays at one while the verdict quietly stops being true.

cases.why: comment stripping is dropped, so a rule retired by commenting it out still counts as a live consumer. The guard then fails on a template that is perfectly fine, and the obvious repair is to edit the guard -- which is how a real second consumer gets waved through later. Two guards in this repo have already counted commented-out markup as present.
